title: Airline agent — may the cabin be changed?
description: Encodes the 'Change cabin' subsection of the Modify flight section of the Airline Agent Policy. Determines whether a requested cabin change is permitted for an existing reservation and, when permitted, whether the price difference is collected from or refunded to the user. Does not cover flight changes, baggage, insurance, passengers, cancellation, or compensation.

decision.intent: Let an airline support agent determine, before touching the booking database, whether a user's request to change the cabin class of an existing reservation is permitted by the Airline Agent Policy, and what the resulting payment or refund consequence is.
decision.question: May the cabin be changed for this reservation, and if so is the price difference collected from or refunded to the user?

evidenceRequirements.description: The user id, provided by the user themselves. The Modify flight section requires the agent to obtain it before any modification is considered.

The reservation id of the reservation whose cabin is to be changed. If the user does not know it, the agent locates it with available tools; either way it must be established before the cabin-change question can be answered.

sources.title: Airline Agent Policy — Modify flight — Change cabin (already-flown restriction)

citation.excerpt: Cabin cannot be changed if any flight in the reservation has already been flown.

sources.title: Airline Agent Policy — Modify flight — Change cabin (general permission)

citation.excerpt: In other cases, all reservations, including basic economy, can change cabin without changing the flights.

sources.title: Airline Agent Policy — Modify flight — Change cabin (cabin uniform across segments)

citation.excerpt: Cabin class must remain the same across all the flights in the same reservation; changing cabin for just one flight segment is not possible.

sources.title: Airline Agent Policy — Modify flight — Change cabin (user pays the difference)

citation.excerpt: If the price after cabin change is higher than the original price, the user is required to pay for the difference.

sources.title: Airline Agent Policy — Modify flight — Change cabin (user is refunded the difference)

citation.excerpt: If the price after cabin change is lower than the original price, the user is should be refunded the difference.

sources.title: Airline Agent Policy — Modify flight (identification preamble)

citation.excerpt: First, the agent must obtain the user id and reservation id. - The user must provide their user id. - If the user doesn't know their reservation id, the agent should help locate it using available tools.

sources.title: Airline Agent Policy — transfer to a human agent

citation.excerpt: You should transfer the user to a human agent if and only if the request cannot be handled within the scope of your actions.

outcomes.label: Cabin change refused
outcomes.description: The cabin change is not permitted by the Change cabin subsection. The agent denies the request; the policy does not direct a transfer to a human agent for this ground.

outcomes.label: Cabin change permitted — collect the price difference
outcomes.description: The cabin change is permitted and the price after the cabin change is higher than the original price, so the user is required to pay the difference.

outcomes.label: Cabin change permitted — refund the price difference
outcomes.description: The cabin change is permitted and the price after the cabin change is lower than the original price, so the user is to be refunded the difference.

outcomes.label: Cabin change permitted — no payment or refund
outcomes.description: The cabin change is permitted and the price after the cabin change equals the original price, so neither the pay-the-difference nor the refund-the-difference clause is triggered and no money moves.

rules.description: When the cabin change is otherwise permitted and the price after the cabin change is higher than the original price, permit the change and collect the difference from the user.
rules.rationale: Bullet 2 grants the permission for every reservation, including basic economy; bullet 4 attaches the payment consequence when the new price is higher. If the direction of the price difference cannot be established the money consequence cannot be stated, so the pack escalates rather than guessing.

rules.description: When the cabin change is otherwise permitted and the price after the cabin change is lower than the original price, permit the change and refund the difference to the user.
rules.rationale: Bullet 2 grants the permission; bullet 5 attaches the refund consequence when the new price is lower. Unknown price direction escalates for the same reason as the collect rule.

rules.description: When the cabin change is otherwise permitted and the price after the cabin change equals the original price, permit the change with no payment and no refund.
rules.rationale: Bullet 2 permits the change and the subsection states no consequence when the two prices are equal: bullet 4 is conditioned on 'higher' and bullet 5 on 'lower', so neither fires. The permission still stands, so the pack states the permission with no money movement rather than leaving the case unresolved.

exceptions.description: Bullet 1 carves this case out of the general permission in bullet 2: if any flight in the reservation has already been flown, the cabin cannot be changed, whatever the price consequence would have been.

Bullet 3 forbids a cabin change scoped to fewer than all the flights in the reservation: cabin class must remain the same across all flights, and changing cabin for just one flight segment is not possible.

escalation.message: The cabin-change question could not be resolved from the facts and evidence supplied. The Change cabin subsection names no ground for a transfer on its own, so this handoff exists only for the case where the request cannot be handled within the scope of the automated agent's actions.
